parts.html: The K-08 standard model is a minimalist straight kitchen in brown tones, where an expressive wood texture meets clean geometry and modern furniture hardware.

The wood-effect decor brings warmth and a natural feel to the interior while preserving the understated character of a modern kitchen. This finish pairs harmoniously with light walls, stone textures, neutral flooring, and minimalist furniture.

The main feature of the K-08 model is the combination of a straight layout and fronts made of HPL-faced MDF panels. The upper and lower cabinets share the same wood aesthetic, giving the furniture composition a cohesive look.

The straight layout places the kitchen furniture along one wall, leaving open space for a dining set. At 4.2 linear meters, the kitchen is well suited to an apartment, a studio, or a modern private home.
The chipboard-based countertop complements the model’s design and provides a work surface for everyday cooking. The carcass is made of 18 mm laminated chipboard.

FREE SPACE Hafele lift-up mechanisms provide easy access to the upper cabinets. Muller Profi Line hinges with soft-close mechanisms ensure smooth door closing, while Muller Box Profi Line drawers help keep kitchen utensils organized.
The kitchen is designed for built-in appliances. With no island or cargo pull-out, the kitchen keeps a simple, functional layout.
Hinges: Muller Profi Line with soft-close mechanisms
DUMSKAYA DESIGN makes modern custom kitchens for apartments, condos, and private homes in Bratislava and Vienna.
The K-08 standard model can be adapted to the dimensions of a specific room, taking into account the location of utility lines and built-in appliances, as well as the client’s individual wishes.
We offer kitchen furniture design, material selection, manufacturing, delivery, and professional installation.
At the client’s request, the kitchen can also be fitted with a sink, appliances, a range hood, and plumbing fixtures.
To order the K-08 kitchen or get a personalized price quote, contact DUMSKAYA DESIGN.
